status_summary: No new executive order stating a general no-degree rule was found. Executive Order 14170, signed 2025-01-20, directs a Federal Hiring Plan with technical and alternative assessments and does not mention degree requirements. The Merit Hiring Plan memorandum of 2025-05-29 states that agencies shall revamp position descriptions and eliminate requirements that are not relevant, such as degree requirements, and cites Executive Order 13932 of 2020 as having directed OPM to remove unnecessary degree requirements. A trade publication in April 2026 reported that OPM was reviewing more than 600 job classifications for possible removal of degree requirements, with agencies still rewriting qualification standards.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14170, Reforming the Federal Hiring Process and Restoring Merit to Government Service, was signed (published 2025-01-30, document 2025-02094); section 2(b)(iii) calls for technical and alternative assessments, and the order does not address degree requirements.

The Merit Hiring Plan memorandum was issued by the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy and the Acting Director of OPM; section II.A states that agencies shall revamp position descriptions and eliminate requirements that are not relevant, such as degree requirements, with no deadline.

title: Executive order: no college degree required for federal jobs unless the job demands it
uncertainties: Searches run: two by the researcher (opm.gov, federalregister.gov and trade-press terms on degree requirements, Executive Order 13932 and the Merit Hiring Plan); the reviewer ran none and re-read the memorandum, the order and the trade article. Executive Order 13932 (signed 2020-06-26) limited minimum education requirements to cases where legally required, per the CRS Insight; the 2025 memorandum cites it as a standing direction, and no revocation was found, but its status was not confirmed on the Federal Register. The 600-classification figure comes from a trade publication that does not cite an OPM document for it. The memorandum's degree language sits inside a broader skills-based hiring directive with no deadline. c03-05 covers skills-based assessments; this record is the degree-requirement element only. In the 2026-10-17 review the memorandum was re-read in full on opm.gov: its signatories are the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy and the Acting OPM Director, section II.A uses mandatory language for agencies to drop irrelevant requirements such as degree requirements, section I lists eliminating unnecessary degree requirements as a key element, and no deadline is set. EO 14170 appears at 90 FR 8621, and its section 2(a) set a 120-day deadline for the Federal Hiring Plan (per the researcher's reading of the Federal Register).
